stem: In which year was ‘Jana Gana Mana’ adopted as the National Anthem of India?
expl: The Constituent Assembly accepted ‘Jana Gana Mana’ as the National Anthem of India on 24 January, 1950. A formal rendition of the national anthem takes fifty-two seconds.

stem: When the Hindi version of National Anthem Jana-Gana-Mana was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India?
expl: The song Jana-Gana-Mana, composed originally in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore, was adopted in its Hindi version by the Constituent Assembly as the National Anthem of India on 24 January 1950. It was first sung on 27th December, 1911 at the Calcutta session of Indian National Congress.

stem: A complete or formal rendition of national anthem takes-
expl: ‘Jan Gana Mana’ is the National Anthem of India, and its formal rendition takes approximately 52 seconds while a shortened version consisting of the first and the last line takes 20 seconds to play.

stem: The state emblem was adopted by Govt. of India on -
expl: The State Emblem which is extracted from the Ashoka pillar at Sarnath (Varanasi) was adopted by the Government of India on 26 January, 1950.

stem: When did the Constituent Assembly adopt the National Flag?
expl: The National Flag of India was adopted during the fourth session of the Constituent Assembly on 22 July, 1947.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The design of the National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on 22nd July, 1947
2. The wheel in National Flag has 21 spokes
3. The ratio of the width of the National Flag to its length is 3 : 4
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
expl: The design of the National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July, 1947. Therefore, statement 1 is correct. There are 24 spokes in the wheel and the width- to length ratio is 2:3. So, statements 2 and 3 are wrong.

stem: Indian National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on which date ?
expl: The Constituent Assembly of India adopted the National Flag of India on 22nd July 1947. The national flag has 24 spokes in the wheel (Ashoka Chakra) in the centre, and the proportion of the length to the width of the flag is 3:2.

stem: On which of the following dates, Constituent Assembly of India adopted the National Flag?
expl: The National Flag is rectangular and consists of three colours. The ratio of the length of the Flag to its width is 3:2. The constituent assembly adopted the National Flag's present design on 22nd July, 1947.

stem: On which day the design of the National flag of India was adopted?
expl: The National Flag is rectangular and consists of three colours. The ratio of the length of the Flag to its width is 3:2. The constituent assembly adopted the National Flag's present design on 22nd July, 1947.

stem:
Consider the following statements in respect of the National Flag of India according to the Flag Code of India, 2002:
Statement-I : One of the standard sizes of the National Flag of India is 600 mm × 400 mm.
Statement-II : The ratio of the length to the height (width) of the Flag shall be 3:2.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.label: a
options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I

options.label: b
options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I

options.label: c
options.text: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

options.label: d
options.text: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

expl: The Flag Code of India 2002 allowed the unrestricted display of the Tricolour as long as the honour and the dignity of the flag was being respected. It takes effect from January 26, 2002. For the sake of convenience, it is divided into three parts - 1. General description of the tricolour, 2. Rules on display of the flag by public and private bodies and educational institutions, 3. Rules for the display of the flag by governments and government bodies. According to the provision of the code, the National Flag shall be rectangular in shape and the ratio of the length to the height (width) of the Flag shall be 3:2. The standard sizes of the National Flag shall be as follows : Flag Size No. Dimensions in mm Hence, statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.

The Tiger (Panthera tigris) is the national animal of India. To improve the decreasing population and to protect tigers, the Tiger Conservation Project was started in April 1973.

stem: Which is the National Flower of India?
expl: Lotus is the national flower of India and is the emblem of Indian Culture. Its scientific name is 'Nelumbo nucifera'.

The national bird of India is the Indian Peacock. Its scientific name is Pavo cristatus. It is notable that Banyan is the national tree, Mango is the national fruit, ‘Satyamev Jayte’ is the national motto taken from Mundaka Upanishad and inscribed in the script at the base of the National Emblem which has been adopted from the Lion Capital of Ashoka erected at Sarnath, Varanasi. The Ganges River Dolphin is the national aquatic animal of India.

stem: What does the wheel on the ‘Indian National Flag’ symbolize?
expl: The wheel on a white strip of National Flag having 24 spokes is adopted from the Ashok Chakra, which is a depiction of Dharmachakra represented by 24 spokes. It symbolizes the wheel of Law. So, Justice is the correct Answer.
